target.title: fix(searxng): fail closed on unresolved base url refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SearXNG lets users configure `plugins.entries.searxng.config.webSearch.baseUrl` as a SecretRef. When that configured SecretRef could not be resolved locally, runtime resolution could still fall through to the ambient `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` environment variable. That could silently route `web_search` requests to a different SearXNG host than the explicitly configured one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured credential-like values should either resolve to the configured target or fail closed. This keeps the SearXNG base URL contract aligned with provider-local SecretRef behavior: ambient env fallback is only for the unconfigured case, not for a configured-but-unavailable SecretRef. A blocked configured value now reports an actionable error instead of incorrectly saying that no base URL was configured.

## User Impact

Users with a valid configured string or env SecretRef keep the same behavior. Users with no configured `baseUrl` can still rely on `SEARXNG_BASE_URL`. Users with an unavailable, blank, null, or malformed configured value now stop before network access and are told to fix or remove the explicit config instead of silently using an unrelated ambient endpoint.

## Evidence

- Added local config matrix coverage for configured string precedence, ambient-env fallback when unconfigured, env SecretRef resolution, missing env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, non-env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, blank/null/malformed value handling, and actionable diagnostics.
- Updated `docs/tools/searxng-search.md` so the documented resolution order matches the runtime contract.
- Exhaustive caller search shows production resolution is used by `runSearxngSearch`; provider auto-detection uses contract metadata and does not call this throwing resolver.
- Related #104216 touches SearXNG client/provider abort handling, not this config resolver.

## Proof

- Exact pushed head: `cad35ada6aa5a280a09b9bb1636053721da9c0e4`.
- The branch merged OpenClaw main at `26e05c1c56d30f6105725bf7cefd0af634307487`. The sole conflict was generated `docs/docs_map.md`; regenerating it resolved the conflict and left no docs-map diff relative to that main. The resulting PR diff is four files.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/searxng/src/config.test.ts extensions/searxng/src/searxng-client.test.ts extensions/searxng/src/searxng-search-provider.test.ts` passed: 3 files, 32 tests.
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed.
- `oxfmt` completed on the touched source/test files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Final Claude autoreview of the synchronized result passed with no accepted/actionable findings. An earlier review finding about the misleading blocked-state error was accepted and fixed before the clean rerun.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox proof was unavailable because no trusted Crabbox/Testbox binary is installed in this environment. Exact-head GitHub CI is the remote validation path for this push.

The deliberate compatibility decision remains with the maintainer: explicitly configured but unavailable values no longer fall through to ambient `SEARXNG_BASE_URL`.
